changes_vs_current: New topic. Scope: US sit-down/full-service chains only (casual, family and polished-casual dining incl. breakfast diners like IHOP/Denny's/Waffle House, buffets like Golden Corral, and eatertainment like Dave & Buster's); counter-service and fast casual excluded (Braum's dropped from the FSR list; First Watch kept eligible but missed the cut). Ranked by average position over four people sources (YouGov Q3 2025 popularity, YouGov 2026 casual-dining consideration, Technomic/FSR sales, Wikipedia pageviews), missing = list length + 5. All 12 gut-check answers landed in the computed top 12. Moves: Applebee's raised from computed #6 to #4 (gut check and YouGov 2026 consideration #3 and 65+ #3; it was dragged down only by Wikipedia views); TGI Fridays raised from #20 to #16 (household name with YouGov 52% popularity and 137k pageviews; it is missing from the sales list only because its US footprint shrank after the 2024 bankruptcy) and Hard Rock Cafe kept just behind it because its Wikipedia views are inflated by the Hard Rock hotel/casino brand. Hooters stays #13 despite topping Wikipedia (bankruptcy news) since it is low on sales and absent from both polls.
confidence: High for #1-#12: the same twelve chains top every source, all with 3-4 people sources, and they match the gut check; exact order within #4-#11 is medium (IHOP, Cheesecake Factory, Cracker Barrel, Outback, Red Lobster and Denny's are separated by small margins and swap depending on source). Medium for #13-#17 (Hooters, LongHorn, Red Robin, TGI Fridays, Hard Rock Cafe): each has 2-3 sources but they disagree strongly (LongHorn big in sales, weak in fame; Hooters/Hard Rock the opposite). Low for #18-#24 (P.F. Chang's, Golden Corral, Benihana, Dave & Buster's, BJ's, Bob Evans, Bubba Gump), which rest on 1-2 sources; Benihana and Bubba Gump lean on Wikipedia alone. Near misses: Ruth's Chris, Cheddar's, Twin Peaks, Ruby Tuesday, Rainforest Cafe, Carrabba's, Buca di Beppo, Friendly's. The YouGov 2026 order is inferred from a countdown article (only the top 3 and #10 are explicit). No ACSI scores were readable beyond Texas Roadhouse #1 and LongHorn #2 in satisfaction.
